narrative.overview:
The app is a dark window at night. The voice draws a gold thread across it, and a band of candlelight shows where the person chose to aim. The past stays still and only the tip moves. It is built for someone alone in a quiet room, glancing at the screen while making sound, so it stays calm, steady and readable from arm's length.

The screen is a stage and a rail: compact and dense, with thin rules and tonal layers. It has no card grid, no gauge and no needle. A small bunny in a witch hat and a row of moons carry the character. Showing up is marked by a moon filling, never by a streak.

The only continuous motion is the trace. Everything else eases in once and stops.
keyCharacteristics: Aubergine night, gold for what is live and primary, lavender second, pink rare.
A permanent stage: trace frame, readout gutter and a strip under the canvas.
Nothing moves when sound comes and goes.
Meaning is always carried by shape and words as well as colour.
Fully local: two bundled fonts, inline SVG, a canvas trace.

rules.name: The Rare Pink Rule
rules.body: Pink marks a moment that needs attention, and only as a small icon: the rest break and the stop heading. It never fills a surface, colours running text, or decorates. The permanent safety line under the controls stays muted, so pink keeps its meaning.

rules.name: The Own Range Rule
rules.body: The only reading whose colour changes is live pitch, and it changes against the person's own range: gold in the band, plain text above or below it. Brightness is always plain text, so it can never read as praise. Other gold numbers hold one colour at every value, so gold on a number never grades it.

rules.name: The One File Rule
rules.body: Every colour lives in `tokens.css`. Components name a token and never a raw hex. Text holds 4.5:1 and graphics 3:1 on every surface, in both themes.

rules.name: The Mono Measurement Rule
rules.body: Live readings, scores and the target range are mono with tabular digits. Timers and recording lengths keep tabular digits in the sans. Readouts always hold four characters, so a number can never change width.

rules.name: The Two Atkinson Rule
rules.body: Only the two Atkinson families are used, and both are bundled with the app. No font ever loads from a network.

rules.name: The Clear Window Rule
rules.body: Nothing covers the band or the thread. Notices, alerts and a session's notes live in the strip. The result takes the readings' place in the gutter, so the thread just drawn stays in view.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The strip says one thing at a time: clipping, louder and the rest reminder first, then an alert, then the neutral notices, then a finished session's notes. A rest reminder that has waited 30 seconds takes the strip for its ten seconds, then the others come back. Away from Practice it uses the alert row. With nothing to say the strip shows a quiet strip of night sky.

rules.name: The Reserved Slot Rule
rules.body: Everything on the practice stage that can change has its size kept in advance: the strip, the status (three lines), the instruction, the safety line and the readout. A notice arriving moves nothing, and the zone only changes once the new zone has lasted, so the status never flickers. A long result scrolls inside the gutter.

rules.name: The Small Window Rule
rules.body: At 800x600 the instruction and safety line stay fully readable in English and Spanish, and the onboarding safety step fits one screen, in Spanish too. Tests cap instructions at 150 characters and strip text at 190. New copy keeps inside those limits.

rules.name: The Candle Light Rule
rules.body: Glow belongs to the trace. It marks the voice being in the band and appears nowhere else.

dos: Do keep every notice, alert and note in the strip and every result in the gutter.
Do reserve the space for anything that can appear on the practice stage before it appears.
Do pair every colour meaning with a drawn mark and words.
Do use the moon strip to show practice. A gap is a new moon and not a loss.
Do keep the safety line and instructions readable at 800x600 in English and Spanish.
Do check new layouts stacked, down to 400x300.
Do honour reduced motion in anything that moves.
Do keep wording plain and free of medical promises. The app measures sound and cannot judge a throat or a voice.
donts: Don't put anything over the band or the thread.
Don't use pink for anything but the two attention icons, and don't add new pink moments lightly.
Don't colour a reading against anything but the person's own range, and don't give brightness the accent.
Don't put a coloured stripe down the side of a notice. Neutral 1px rules between regions are fine.
Don't add streaks, streak counts or any language of loss.
Don't load remote assets or fonts, and don't add raster art. Art is inline SVG, and the trace is canvas.
Don't add glows beyond the trace, or glass, or a second continuous motion.
